Code reference¶

Models¶

Database models for the news application.

Normalisation notes (see DESIGN.md for the full ERD):

  • Every non-key column depends only on its table’s primary key (3NF).

  • Many-to-many relationships (editors, journalists, subscriptions and newsletter contents) live in Django-managed link tables instead of comma-separated columns.

  • “Independent” articles are not stored separately: an article with no publisher is independent, so the information is never duplicated.

Role groups and permissions¶

Role names, group names and the permissions each role’s group receives.

This module deliberately imports nothing from news.models so that the models can import it without creating a circular import.

ROLE_GROUP_NAMES maps a role value ("reader", "editor", "journalist") to its group name, and ROLE_PERMISSIONS lists the permission codenames each group receives.

news.groups.setup_role_groups()[source]¶

Create the three role groups and assign their permissions.

Safe to run repeatedly: groups are fetched or created and their permission sets are replaced with the definitions above. It runs automatically after every migrate (see news.signals).

Returns:

None.

class news.permissions.ContentPermission[source]¶

Role-based access for articles and newsletters in the API.

  • Anyone authenticated can read.

  • Only journalists can create (POST).

  • Editors and journalists can update/delete; a journalist is limited to their own items (checked per object).

Check the request method against the user’s role.

Allow reads, but restrict writes to editors and the owner.

Queries¶

Reusable article queries shared by the web views and the REST API.

news.queries.article_queryset()[source]¶

Return the base article queryset.

Authors and publishers are fetched in the same query (select_related) so list pages do not run one extra query per article.

Returns:

a queryset of news.models.Article.

news.queries.approved_articles()[source]¶

Return every article an editor has approved.

Returns:

a queryset of approved news.models.Article objects, newest first.

news.queries.subscribed_articles(user)[source]¶

Approved articles from the publishers/journalists a reader follows.

Users who are not readers have no subscriptions, so they get nothing. An article matching both a publisher and a journalist subscription is returned only once.

Parameters:

user – the (authenticated) user whose subscriptions to use.

Returns:

a queryset of approved articles, possibly empty.

Notifications and signals¶

Side effects that run when an article is approved.

Kept separate from the signal handlers so the logic is easy to test and to reuse from a view if the signal approach is ever swapped for “Option 2”.

news.services.get_subscriber_emails(article)[source]¶

Return e-mail addresses of readers following the article’s source.

A reader qualifies if they subscribe to the article’s author or to its publisher (when it has one). Readers without an address are skipped.

Parameters:

article – the approved news.models.Article.

Returns:

a list of unique e-mail address strings (possibly empty).

Return type:

list[str]

news.services.send_approval_email(article)[source]¶

E-mail the approved article to its subscribers.

Delivery errors are logged rather than raised so a mail outage cannot block an editor’s approval. Subscribers are blind-copied so they cannot see each other’s addresses.

Parameters:

article – the approved news.models.Article.

Returns:

the number of recipients e-mailed (0 if there were none or the mail could not be sent).

Return type:

int

news.services.build_approval_payload(article)[source]¶

Return the JSON-serialisable dict sent to /api/approved/.

Parameters:

article – the approved news.models.Article.

Returns:

a dict with the article id, title, content, author and publisher names, approving editor and creation time.

Return type:

dict

news.services.post_approved_article(article)[source]¶

POST the approved article to our own RESTful endpoint.

Network problems are logged, not raised, so approval never fails because the endpoint is unreachable.

Parameters:

article – the approved news.models.Article.

Returns:

True if the endpoint accepted the POST, otherwise False (also when APPROVED_API_URL is empty).

Return type:

bool

Signal handlers (implementation strategy “Option 1” from the brief).

  • pre_save/post_save on Article detect the moment an article becomes approved and trigger the e-mail and the POST to /api/approved/.

  • m2m_changed keeps reader subscriptions reader-only.

  • create_role_groups builds the Reader/Editor/Journalist groups.

news.signals.create_role_groups(sender, **kwargs)[source]¶

post_migrate handler: create role groups and their permissions.

news.signals.remember_previous_approval(sender, instance, **kwargs)[source]¶

Record whether the article was already approved before this save.

news.signals.handle_article_approval(sender, instance, raw=False, **kwargs)[source]¶

Notify subscribers when an article changes to approved.

Saving an already-approved article again does nothing, so editing the text later never re-sends the e-mail.

Web (HTML) views for the news application.

Access control uses Django’s permission system: each role’s group holds the model permissions defined in news/groups.py and the views check them with PermissionRequiredMixin. Object-level rules (a journalist may only change their own work) are enforced in get_object.

Validates the body POSTed to /api/approved/ by the signal.

REST API views.

Endpoints (all under /api/):

POST token/ obtain an auth token GET articles/ approved articles GET articles/subscribed/ approved articles a reader follows GET articles/<id>/ one article POST articles/ create (journalists) PUT articles/<id>/ update (editors / owner journalist) DELETE articles/<id>/ delete (editors / owner journalist) POST approved/ log an approved article (internal)
